title: Windsor police officer doing homeless outreach morning of Mahoney's shooting death: Inquest
article: A Taser, police commands and the arrival of several cruisers did not deter a man swinging a knife at an injured officer, so Const. Andre Marentette made a split-second decision: he shot the person several times.

Marentette, who testified about the fatal interaction Tuesday in the inquest into the death of 33-year-old Matthew Mahoney, wasn't originally the Windsor police officer tasked with responding to a report of a man with a knife block in the downtown core on March 21, 2018.
Marentette said he and a social worker were conducting outreach with the local homeless population when the call came in.
Believing the description matched someone Marentette had spoken to that morning while doing outreach, he decided to respond.
But a short time later, one officer had been stabbed in the hand and Mahoney was shot. Both were taken to hospital and Mahoney was pronounced dead later that morning.

The inquest into Mahoney's death continued Tuesday with lengthy testimony from Marentette and a review of surveillance camera footage showing the altercation between police and Mahoney and the subsequent shooting.

Mahoney was first spotted walking around University and Ouellette avenues around 8 a.m. March 21, 2018 carrying a knife block with eight knives, according to a call to the Windsor police non-emergency line placed by a manager of the Starbucks at that intersection. Officers were dispatched and Marentette responded.

Marentette said multiple attempts to verbally engage with Mahoney, made by himself and another officer, weren't successful and Mahoney started advancing on the officer with a knife out, making slashing motions while the officer backed away and fell to the ground. Marentette said he saw the discharged Taser on the ground but noted it had not worked.

He told the jury he then made the decision that the situation had moved beyond the use of non-lethal force because communication, a Taser, officers' physical movements and the presence of multiple police cruisers had not deterred Mahoney.
"There was nothing getting his attention" away from the officer on the ground, Marentette said, adding he understood the officer was injured.
Marentette told the jury he fired his gun multiple times, the third and fourth shots bringing Mahoney to the ground. Marentette said he disarmed Mahoney and started providing aid.
When medical personnel arrived on the scene, Marentette testified he had the impression they weren't aware someone had been shot and he called them over to provide aid to Mahoney.

Marentette also answered questions Tuesday about the police training he received, the sequence of events that morning and his experience working with people with mental health challenges. Inquest counsel, the Mahoney family and counsel for both Windsor police and Marentette personally questioned Marentette in a bid to elicit details about the other officers on scene and the evidence recovered from the scene.

A Special Investigations Unit investigation has previously cleared Windsor police of wrongdoing in Mahoney's death. The five-member jury in this inquest will aim to answer the questions of who Mahoney was, where and when he died, and the cause and manner of his death. They may also provide recommendations to prevent similar deaths in the future.

The five-member jury also heard from two other witnesses Tuesday morning: The then-manager at a downtown Starbucks who phoned police non-emergency line reporting Mahoney carrying the knives and a woman who had a brief interaction with Mahoney in the Shopper's Drug Mart parking lot that morning.
